Leonid Andreyev, Satan’s Diary, translated by Herman Bernstein.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/leonid-andreyev/satans-diary/herman-bernstein

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Leonid Andreyev, the author, died 1919 (Wikidata Q310866, P570 = 1919-09-12 and 1919-01-01).
- Herman Bernstein, the translator, died 1935 (Wikidata Q3507116, P570 = 1935-08-31).

First publication of the text used: 1920 for the English translation (the Russian original was published in 1919). SE colophon: 'Satan’s Diary was published in 1919 by Leonid Andreyev. It was translated from Russian in 1920 by Herman Bernstein.'

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1920, before 1931, and the edition's rights statement (quoted below) places it in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin of the English text (not stated in the facts; the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa): each has a copyright term of life plus 70 years or less. The last person to die (Bernstein, 1935) makes the translation public domain in each of them no later than 1 January 2006. Country of origin of the Russian original (1919; the author's country is Russia): for Andreyev, who died in 1919, a term of life plus 70 years ends on 31 December 1989, so the original is in the public domain from 1 January 1990 in Russia and in every other country with a term of life plus 70 years or less. No person named above worked or fought in World War II, so the Russian wartime extension does not apply.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:

- Wikidata Q310866 (Leonid Andreyev), P570 = 1919-09-12 and 1919-01-01.
